summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would repeal the Supported Accommodation Assistance Act 1994 and adjust electoral legislation as part of replacing the Commonwealth's homelessness legislative framework.
It would replace an electoral definition that partly depends on the repealed Act, preserving arrangements for people experiencing homelessness to enrol as itinerant electors.
Its substantive amendments would begin alongside the proposed Homelessness Act 2013, with the revised electoral definition intended to preserve the existing provisions' operation.
changes: The entire Supported Accommodation Assistance Act 1994 would be repealed.
The electoral definition would expressly include people in crisis or transitional accommodation and people lacking adequate access to secure, safe housing.
The electoral definition's reference to the Supported Accommodation Assistance Act would be removed.
summary.affected: People experiencing homelessness, including itinerant electors and people living in crisis or transitional accommodation, are affected.

speeches.speaker: Kevin Andrews
speeches.brief: Argued that the Homelessness Bill 2013 is aspirational and adds no funding, citing a 17 per cent rise in homelessness from 89,728 in 2006 to 105,237 in 2011 despite Labor's pledge to halve it by 2020, criticised a $159 million one-year funding deal as a bandaid, and said a coalition government would provide a $1.5 billion mental health package.

speeches.speaker: Jane Prentice
speeches.brief: Argued that the Homelessness Bill 2013 offers only aspiration without funding, citing a 17 per cent rise in homelessness from 89,728 in 2006 to 105,237 in 2011 despite Labor's pledge to halve it by 2020, and noted the government's $159 million one-year funding deal and pledged a coalition government would provide a $1.5 billion mental health package instead.
